summary.tldr: Requires warning labels on alcoholic beverages and adds information about standard drinks, health risks, and cancer links.
what_it_does: Requires any beverage with 1.1% alcohol by volume or more to be sold in a package with a warning label about the health risks of alcohol consumption.

Requires the label to show the volume that counts as a standard drink, the number of standard drinks in the package, and the number that should not be exceeded to avoid significant health risks, as set by the Department.
Requires the label to include a Department message stating the direct causal link between alcohol consumption and fatal cancers.
Brings the changes into force one year after royal assent.
summary.background: The bill adds a new warning-label rule to the Food and Drugs Act. It would apply to beverages with 1.1% alcohol by volume or more.
